name: Pedro Espíndula
whoAmI: Staff Site Reliability Engineer with 5+ years in SRE at Brazilian fintech and payments companies, focused on observability, incident response and the cost of reliability.

At Cora, rolled out alerting and on-call to 100% of engineering teams, raising alert acknowledgement from 17% to 85% and cutting critical-alert MTTA from 12 to 4 minutes, and consolidated observability onto Datadog for $67K in yearly savings.
At Pagar.me (StoneCo), cut MTTA by 70% and MTTR by 55%.

roles.title: Staff Site Reliability Engineer
mainActivities: Built usage and cost anomaly alerting for every Datadog product, with 105% and 110% thresholds plus per-team cost dashboards, after detecting and containing a log-ingestion burst 400–500x above baseline that had accrued $29.7K; the alerts have since caught 1 further anomaly in custom-metric volume

Root-caused a facial-login failure invisible to error monitors because 100% of responses returned HTTP 200, leading to the fix that cut the failure rate from 80% to 4% and the Android capture-screen p95 from 87s to under 7s
Driving SLOs with active error budgets for the 6 business-critical flows, including Pix instant payments, onboarding, credit, credit card and acquiring

roles.title: Senior Site Reliability Engineer
mainActivities: Cut observability spend by $67K a year by consolidating 3 vendors onto Datadog, decommissioning New Relic and Sentry, and right-sizing the contract and APM ingestion

Raised the alert acknowledgement rate 5x, from 17% to 85%, by rolling out Rootly for alerting and on-call to 100% of engineering teams, with a Go CLI that migrated 1,215 monitors from 4 alerting sources through a dual-write rollout
Selected the on-call platform among 11 vendors through a 3-year TCO analysis and negotiated a 50% discount on on-call licenses, saving $9.5K a year

Cut MTTA on critical alerts by 66%, from 12 to 4 minutes, by establishing incident-management standards (severity taxonomy, incident manager role, blameless postmortems) backed by an SRE health-metrics framework
Doubled Datadog application coverage from 36% to 75% by standardizing monitors, alert channels, permissions and SSO, replacing the access-ticket queue with self-service
Raised on-time postmortems from 21% to 58% with automated reminders, AI-assisted drafting and per-area accountability
Shipped 4 read-only MCP servers (Grafana, Datadog, Superset, Rootly) to production, giving 3 engineering and AI organizations programmatic access to observability data

Mentored 2 junior SREs to own the alerting platform, who went on to handle 52% of inbound platform requests in a quarter without escalation, and ran 11 SRE Office Hours sessions open to all of engineering
